items.q: How does the planning work?
items.a: It starts with a conversation. You can plan every detail with us, or give us a sense of what you would like and we will send a draft itinerary for you to shape. Nothing is booked without your approval.

items.q: Can the trip be fully tailored to us?
items.a: Yes. The sample journeys are there to spark ideas, and nothing in them is fixed. Every trip follows your interests and your pace.

items.q: What does the price include?
items.a: Everything is taken care of: a private driver and transfers, accommodation, meals and dining, guides and experiences, and every booking handled ahead of time, with someone looking after your trip throughout.

items.q: How does pricing work for a group?
items.a: There is no set price. The cost per person depends on your plans and how many of you are travelling. Once we know both, we send a full proposal before anything is booked.

items.q: Why do your sample journeys not show a price?
items.a: The same route can vary widely with the season, the standard of stay, how you travel and how many of you there are. Tell us which journey appeals and we will send a full proposal for it.

items.q: How far ahead should we book?
items.a: As early as you can, especially for summer, when the best rooms and experiences go first. We also plan trips at shorter notice.

items.q: Can you arrange things that are not in your sample itineraries?
items.a: Almost certainly. The samples are only a starting point. Tell us what you have always wanted to do in Scotland, and we will look at building it in.

items.q: What parts of Scotland do you cover?
items.a: All of it, from Edinburgh and the Borders to the Highlands, Skye and the islands, Speyside and the far north. The route follows what you want to see. Scotland is our home, though we can plan beyond it when a trip calls for it.

items.q: Can you look after families, special occasions and particular requirements?
items.a: Yes. We plan for couples, families and groups marking something special. We look after the details that matter to you, from the pace of each day to where you dine.

items.q: Can you get us onto the Old Course at St Andrews?
items.a: The Old Course is allocated mainly through a daily public ballot, so a place can never be guaranteed. We enter the ballot for you and build your St Andrews day around a confirmed round on another of the Links courses. If your name comes up, the Old Course is the bonus.

items.q: How far in advance should we book?
items.a: As early as you can. Most courses open tee times around the autumn before the year you want to play. Booking early gives you the widest choice, especially at the well-known courses in summer. Shorter notice is still workable, with fewer options on the busiest tee sheets.

items.q: Which courses can you arrange?
items.a: We arrange rounds at most of Scotland's championship and best-loved courses. A few can only be played as a member's guest, and we will tell you which at the outset.

items.q: What does a golf tour include?
items.a: From arrival to departure: private transfers, green fees, caddies and clubs where you want them, accommodation chosen for where you play next, meals, and any experiences you would like around the golf.

items.q: How many rounds will we play in a week?
items.a: A typical week runs to four or five rounds, with the other days left for rest, a distillery, sightseeing or whatever suits the group. We set the pace to suit you.

items.q: Do you arrange caddies, clubs and transport between courses?
items.a: Yes. A private driver looks after you for the whole trip, so you are never finding your own way to an early tee time, and we arrange caddies and club hire wherever you would like them.

items.q: Can non-golfers come along?
items.a: Absolutely. We are just as happy planning the days for anyone travelling with you who would rather be at a distillery, a spa, a castle or the coast while the golf is on.

items.q: How much does a Scotland golf tour cost?
items.a: Prices vary a great deal with the courses you choose, the number of rounds, where you stay and the season, so we price every tour individually. Once we know your plans, we put together a full, itemised proposal before anything is booked.

items.q: Do you arrange tours for corporate or company groups?
items.a: Yes. We plan golf trips for companies looking to reward a team or host clients, taking care of the group logistics, the hospitality and the evenings as well as the golf.

items.q: What areas of Scotland do you cover?
items.a: We are based in Glasgow and cover the whole of Scotland, from the cities to the Highlands and islands. That might be a short transfer in town or a day's drive across the country.

items.q: What kind of vehicles do you provide?
items.a: A car to suit your party: an executive saloon for one or two, a larger luxury car or SUV, or a people carrier for a group with luggage. Tell us how many are travelling and what you have planned, and we will match the car to it.

items.q: How many passengers can you take?
items.a: Anything from a single passenger to a group of seven, depending on the vehicle. For larger parties, we can arrange more than one car so everyone travels together.

items.q: Will you meet us at the airport?
items.a: Yes. We meet you on arrival, track your flight in case it lands early or late, and see you and your luggage to the car.

items.q: Can we hire a car and driver for a full day, or longer?
items.a: Yes. Book a car and driver for a day or for several, and explore at your own pace. Your driver takes you wherever you would like to go.

items.q: Do you provide transfers for golf trips and events?
items.a: Yes. We get you between courses, dinners and events comfortably and on time, early tee times included. We drive as part of our golf tours and event services, or for a trip you are running yourself.

items.q: What is included?
items.a: Your driver, the vehicle, fuel and parking, plus meet and greet and flight tracking on airport pickups. Water and refreshments are in the car.

items.q: How far ahead should we book?
items.a: Early, if you can, especially in summer and around major events, when cars are in demand. Shorter notice is often possible, so do ask.

items.q: How far in advance should we start planning?
items.a: The more notice, the more choice, especially for the most sought-after places in summer. For a trip of three days or more, we recommend coming to us four to six months ahead. Shorter timelines are often workable too.

items.q: How many people can you accommodate?
items.a: We work with groups of all sizes, from small leadership teams to company-wide reward trips. Group size shapes the choice of venues and transport, and we will say early if something suits a different scale.

items.q: Can the trip be themed around our company or its goals?
items.a: Yes. If there is a theme, a goal or a message you want the trip to carry, we build it into the days themselves: the welcome, the choice of activities, the way evenings are framed, and the small details that link one day to the next.

items.q: Do you handle everything once the group lands?
items.a: Yes. From the airport welcome to the final transfer home, we plan and run every part of the trip. Flights to Scotland are arranged separately.

items.q: How does pricing work for a corporate trip?
items.a: There is no set figure. We work out a cost per person from the group size, the experiences you choose, where you stay and how you travel. Once we understand your brief, we send a full, itemised proposal before anything is confirmed.

items.q: Can you accommodate a mixed group with different interests?
items.a: Yes. We plan the days so everyone has something they would choose to do. Distillery visits, Highland activities, wildlife, walking, spa time and cultural experiences can all run side by side.

items.q: Can you arrange photography, video or branded elements for the trip?
items.a: Yes. We can arrange a photographer for key moments, branded welcome gifts, printed materials and other touches that make the trip feel like your company's own.

items.q: What if our numbers change between booking and travel?
items.a: We build in flexibility wherever we can and manage changes as they come. Some elements, exclusive-use venues especially, are harder to change at short notice, so we set out what is fixed at the start.

items.q: Do you work with incentive travel agencies as well as directly with companies?
items.a: Yes, we work both ways. If you are coming to us through an agency or working with a travel manager, we are happy to work within that structure. If you are coming to us directly, we handle everything in house from brief to delivery.

items.q: What is a self-guided tour?
items.a: A trip you travel independently, at your own pace and in your own company. We design the route and book the places to stay and the things worth doing. You set off with everything arranged, and we are a phone call away.

items.q: What exactly do you arrange?
items.a: We build the itinerary and book whatever you would like handled: accommodation, restaurants, tastings, activities and experiences. Each day comes with detailed recommendations. We can also add car hire or a private guide for a day.

items.q: Do you provide transport or move our luggage?
items.a: No. You travel in whatever way suits you, with your own luggage. Our part is the planning and the bookings. If you would like a car or a driver for part of the trip, we can arrange it.

items.q: How is this different from planning the trip myself?
items.a: We know which places are worth your time and which to skip, and how to join them into a route that flows. We hold the right rooms and tables before they fill. The trip is shaped around how you like to travel.

items.q: Can we still change things once we are travelling?
items.a: Yes. The pace and the days are yours, and if something needs to shift while you are away, we are on hand to help rework it. A self-guided trip is meant to leave room for spontaneity.

items.q: Can we add a driver or guide for part of the trip?
items.a: At any time. Some people travel the whole route independently, others like a private guide for a particular day or a driver for a stretch they would rather not drive. We can build that in wherever it suits you.

items.q: How far ahead should we book?
items.a: The earlier the better. The best places to stay and the most popular experiences fill well ahead, especially in summer. Shorter notice is still workable.

items.q: How much does a self-guided tour cost?
items.a: There is no set price, since it depends on your route, how long you travel and what you would like us to book. Tell us what you have in mind and we will put together a proposal, with a sample route to show what a trip can look like.

items.q: What does your event management service include?
items.a: We take on the whole event, from the first idea to the last guest leaving. That covers the concept, the venue, the suppliers, the catering, the production and styling, the guest arrangements and the running of it on the day. One team leads all of it.

items.q: What kinds of events do you manage?
items.a: A wide range, from private dinners and celebrations to corporate functions, product launches, awards evenings, gala dinners and charity events. Each is planned around its purpose and its guests.

items.q: What is the difference between event management and event staffing?
items.a: Event management means we run the whole event: the planning, the suppliers, the production and the day itself. Event staffing means we provide the people (front-of-house and hospitality) for an event you or someone else is running. Many clients take both.

items.q: How large or small an event can you manage?
items.a: Anything from a private dinner for twenty to a corporate gathering for several hundred. The care is the same at either size.

items.q: Do you source the venue, or work with one we already have?
items.a: Either. If you need a venue, we find and secure it, whether a country estate, a city hotel or somewhere unexpected. If the venue is already decided, or you came to us through one, we work within it and manage everything around it.

items.q: Who runs the event on the day?
items.a: A dedicated event producer from our team leads it throughout, and the staff and suppliers report to them. You are free to be a guest at your own event.

items.q: Do you manage the suppliers, catering and production as well?
items.a: Yes, all of it under one roof: catering, entertainment, the technical and audiovisual side, the styling and décor, and the timing that holds it together. You deal with us, and we deal with everyone else.

items.q: Can you manage events beyond Scotland?
items.a: Scotland is our home and where most of our events take place. Where an occasion calls for it, we can manage events beyond Scotland too.

items.q: How far ahead should we start planning?
items.a: As early as you can, especially for sought-after venues and busy times of year, which book up well ahead. We can also work to shorter timelines.

items.q: How much does event management cost?
items.a: There is no set price. It depends on the scale, the venue and what the event involves. Tell us about the occasion and we will send a detailed proposal, costed in full, before anything is committed.
